verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 4 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: All seven of my v1 findings are repaired, and I verified each by measurement rather than by reading v2's account of itself. The blocker is the one that mattered: v1 deferred the decision-column fragment 'signing/notarization' in ROW, handing it to DR-112 and DR-110, neither of which carries core signing or OS notarization in its own text. v2 defers it in TIME instead, to a later DR-101 successor, in the same form OD-101-1 already used, and demotes the two rows to adjacent mechanics described in their own register wording. Both v1 sites are fixed, and I swept every DR-112 and DR-110 mention plus all six identityDependencies rides to confirm no equivalent export survives anywhere else. The closed-roster claim is the other thing a repair successor has to get right, and it holds in both directions: 32 changed paths, all rostered, all 17 rostered paths genuinely moved, /date named explicitly. Two repairs are better than what I asked for. On the COORD pin I suggested re-pinning; v2 instead labels the inherited pin, records the live value separately, and re-verifies the four named properties — and when I extracted D-002, D-006, D-056 and D-089 from both revisions they were byte-identical, with the whole drift additive, so the inheritance is not merely disclosed but safe. On the hedges, 'Proposed' was restored only on the one file 02 table cell that carries it, leaving the other two correctly unhedged. The four advisories are presentational or attributional; none asserts anything false, and one of them is that v2 adopted my own gate numbering as if it were D-056's.

I rejected v1, so the basis for the change should be visible: v1 failed on one blocker and four SHOULD-FIX, all seven findings are now repaired, and I re-derived each repair from live bytes instead of trusting the repair roster. Three things the coordinator should carry forward. First, this ACCEPT does not make DR-101 D-056-eligible, and the artifact is now explicit about why not — the remainder is not only execution/measurement while OD-101-1 and OD-101-2 stand as design reservations, so gates 2 and 3 fail. Nothing here is a step toward SATISFIED beyond being a reviewed T2-02 contract for the inventory/layering half. Second, Codex has never reviewed v1 or v2; the artifact says so itself at notFoldedThisSuccessor, and a Codex verdict carrying findings beyond mine would require a v3. My ACCEPT is one lane only. Third, the COORD recorded input is deliberately an inherited v1-authoring pin rather than a live one; that is correct and I verified both the inheritance and its safety, but anyone re-measuring recordedInputs against live bytes will see 12d192f7… against b9819d6e… and should read /reMeasurementAtV2 before treating it as drift.
